full_judgment: 4. Mr. A. M. Amin Uddin, the learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellants submits that the High Court Division issued Rule on 30.11.2004 returnable within 4(four) weeks but before expiry of the returnable date the rule was heard ex-parte on 13.12.2004 to the serious prejudice of the petitioners and, thus, the High Court Division committed an error of law. He further submits that with reference to the revisional application filed before the High Court Division that the application itself being not in form, hence, it was not maintainable and, as such, in an application which itself lacked maintainability, the High Court Division passed the impugned judgment and order at the back of the petitioners and thereby committed an error of law. The Mr. A. M. Amin Uddin then referred to the following observation of the High Court Division "Therefore we find that the learned appellate Court due to omission failed to pass any order in the petition filed by the petitioner under Order 39, Rules 1 and 2 of the Code. Accordingly, we find merit in the Rule". He next submits that the impugned judgment of the High Court Division does not disclose any reasonable ground for passing the said order and, as such, it calls for interference. He further submits that the high Court Division did not consider that the suit land is the Forest Department under the Government of Bangladesh which is controlled and supervised by the Forest Department since 1950 after avulsion of Zaminder system under gazette notification dated 15.12.1953 submits that the High Court Division failed to consider in law as well as facts the possession controlled and management of the Forest Department since 1950. Now the suit land is under the guidance of Asian Development Bank (ADB) there was a share of landless peoples and after in the year 1956, nobody has no right save and accept the Forest Department and, as such, the impugned and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set aside.
